text:
Code context for people and agents. 
 Find a function’s callers. Trace the path through your code. 
 Know what breaks before you break it.
 

 
 arbor retirements finds direct OpenAI, Anthropic and Google SDK calls in Python code that use a retired or retiring model, and says what has to change. 
 OpenAI shuts down the dated gpt-4o and gpt-4.1 snapshots on 14 January 2027. Shutdown list 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 Simulated replay — the arbor commands and their output are real (tokio @ 178k LOC). Methodology: BENCHMARKS.md 
 

 v3.1.1 · A fix release. The arbor retirements data was read again on 28 October 2026 and now lists the bare gpt-5 and o3 , which OpenAI's deprecations page gives 11 December 2026. npx @anandb71/arbor-cli runs on npm 12, and Arbor no longer takes your home folder as the project because /.arbor exists. Release notes

---

 Why Arbor

Most AI coding tools treat code as text. Arbor builds a semantic dependency graph — functions, classes, and modules as nodes; calls, imports, and inheritance as edges — then answers execution-aware questions with deterministic precision:

 Question Arbor answer 
 ---------- -------------- 
 If I change this symbol, what breaks? Blast radius with depth, confidence, and risk level 
 Who calls this — directly and transitively? Caller/callee traversal on the call graph 
 What's the shortest path between A and B? A path through real dependencies 
 Is this PR too risky to merge? CI gate on blast-radius thresholds 

No keyword guessing. No embedding hallucinations. One graph, every interface.

Where the graph is unsure , it says so — edges carry a confidence, and ambiguous resolutions are labelled rather than hidden. An honest unknown beats a confident wrong answer.

---

 What's new in v3.1.1

A fix release. No breaking changes; as after every upgrade, a saved graph is
rebuilt once on first use.

 Fix What was wrong 
 ----- ---------------- 
 Bare gpt-5 and o3 OpenAI's deprecations page started listing bare IDs next to the dated snapshots after 3.1.0 was built, so model="gpt-5" or model="o3" was not listed at all. Both are listed now (11 December 2026, to GPT-5.6), with the 13 other IDs the page added. 
 Data read again on 28 October 2026 Every provider page behind the bundled data was read and checked again. OpenAI's deprecations page lists the five dated gpt-4o , gpt-4o-mini , gpt-4.1 and gpt-4.1-mini snapshots for 14 January 2027; for the bare aliases the report now cites OpenAI's API reference ("Deprecated. Announced shutdown date: 2027-01-14") and its models API. A call moving to claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 with temperature now gets a check line: Anthropic's API version 2026-10-21 rejects it on every model. 
 (no change) next to arguments that need reasoning off For a call whose client Arbor could not resolve, temperature , tools or max tokens went unchecked and "let the model reason" read (no change) . They are checked now. When Arbor cannot read some of a call's arguments ( kwargs , extra body ) or a check line names one of them, each option says so instead of no change . 
 npx on npm 12 npm 12 skips install scripts, so the binary was never downloaded. The wrapper now downloads it on first run and checks it against the release's SHA256SUMS . 
 The home folder as the project /.arbor holds the global config (and, on Windows, the installed binary), so a folder under home with no nearer project marker resolved to the whole home folder, and arbor index . indexed all of it. The search now stops at the home folder. 
 Code graph: aliased imports and bare calls After from m import f as g , a call to g() now reaches f (also for import { f as g } in TypeScript and JavaScript). In Python, JavaScript, TypeScript and Go, a bare call to a function in another file counts only when the calling file can see it (in Python, when it imports the name); other languages are unchanged. 

When the terminal report of arbor retirements lists a call to a retired or
retiring model, it now ends with an offer of a paid readiness review. The link
carries three values from the run: how many calls are listed, how many are
already retired and the next shutdown date. Arbor sends nothing. The offer is not
printed with --json , --markdown , --annotations or --quiet , or when the CI 
environment variable is set (GitHub Actions sets it), and the GitHub Action does
not show it. Release notes

 
 v3.1.0 ( arbor retirements and arbor usages ) 

Two commands for Python code that calls AI model APIs. Both run locally, with no
account, API key or telemetry.

 New What it does 
 ----- -------------- 
 arbor retirements Lists the direct openai , anthropic and Google SDK calls that use a model its provider has retired or is retiring: the date, the replacement the provider lists, the arguments that change with it and the choices your repo makes first. OpenAI's deprecations page lists the dated gpt-4o , gpt-4o-mini , gpt-4.1 and gpt-4.1-mini snapshots for shutdown on 14 January 2027; OpenAI's API reference and models API give the bare aliases the same date. More below 
 GitHub Action mode: retirements The same check in CI: a job summary of the affected calls it finds, and warnings on the most urgent lines. It warns by default and fails the build only when you set retirements-fail-on , or when the check cannot run. 
 arbor usages and find api usages The OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini SDK calls Arbor finds, with their file and line, client routing (direct, Azure, custom base url , Bedrock, Vertex) and model IDs, for people and agents. A value is confirmed only inside a small supported grammar; everything else carries a typed gap. What a report confirms 

Python only for now. Release notes

 

 
 v3.0.3 (Rust calls through paths and macros, per-symbol diff, --base ) 

A fix release. Every item below was a wrong answer, not a missing feature, and
each ships with a regression test.

 Fix What was wrong 
 ----- ---------------- 
 Rust calls resolve crate::jobs::enqueue() , Type::new() , s

install.title: Quickstart
install.html:
# Install (crates.io can lag the latest release: see docs/INSTALL.md)
cargo install arbor-graph-cli

# Index your project (one command)
cd your-project && arbor setup

# Explore before you edit
arbor map . --exclude-test          # ranked project skeleton (~1k tokens)
arbor refactor parse_file           # blast radius of changing a symbol
arbor diff                          # impact of uncommitted git changes
arbor diff --base origin/main       # impact of this branch, as its PR shows it

# Wire up your AI agent
claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope project arbor -- arbor bridge

After every turn: arbor hook claude makes Claude Code show a receipt of what it changed, what it touched that you didn't ask for, and what to test. Receipts →

Agent workflow: call get_map first → search_symbols / get_file_graph to locate code → Read only the target file. Full MCP guide →
